title: Slow Cooker Tomato, White Bean & Rice Soup
description: Tomatoes, white beans, carrots, and rice simmer into an inexpensive hands-off pantry soup.
substitutions: Use chickpeas instead of white beans.
Use frozen mixed vegetables instead of carrots.
Use brown rice only if you can allow extra cooking time.

steps.text: Cook until the rice and carrots are tender.

cookSteps.text: Add 2 cans drained white beans, 1 can diced tomatoes, 4 cups broth, 2 sliced carrots, 1/2 cup uncooked rice, 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder to the slow cooker. Stir well.
Cover and cook on HIGH for about 4 hours, until the rice and carrots are tender.
Stir well before serving. Add a splash of broth or water if you prefer a thinner soup.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. The rice will absorb broth, so add a splash of water or broth when reheating.

title: Sheet-Pan Broccoli, Potato & Cheddar Bowls
description: Roasted potatoes and broccoli get a simple cheddar finish for an easy meatless sheet-pan dinner.
substitutions: Use sweet potatoes instead of regular potatoes.
Use Monterey Jack instead of cheddar.

steps.text: Add broccoli and finish with cheese.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss 1 1/2 pounds cubed potatoes with 1 tablespoon oil, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/2 teaspoon salt on a large sheet pan.
Toss 4 cups broccoli with the remaining 1 tablespoon oil, add it to the pan, and roast 12–15 minutes more until everything is tender and browned.
Sprinkle 1 cup cheddar over the hot vegetables and return to the oven for 1–2 minutes, just until melted. Divide into bowls.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat in the oven, toaster oven, or microwave.

title: Leftover Rice, Ham & Pea Skillet
description: Cold leftover rice, deli ham, peas, and egg become a fast skillet meal with ordinary refrigerator staples.
substitutions: Use chopped deli turkey instead of ham.
Use frozen mixed vegetables instead of peas.
Skip the soy sauce and season with salt and pepper instead.

steps.text: Heat the rice, ham, and peas.
Scramble in the eggs and finish.

cookSteps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon oil or butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 cup diced ham and 1 cup frozen peas; cook 2 minutes.
Add 3 cups cold cooked rice and cook 4–5 minutes, stirring and breaking up clumps, until hot.
Push the rice aside, crack in 2 eggs, and scramble until set. Stir everything together with 1 tablespoon soy sauce if using and cook 1–2 minutes more.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Small-Batch Peach Oat Crumble
description: A couple of peaches bake under a buttery cinnamon-oat topping for a small, uncomplicated dessert.

ingredients.item: sliced peaches, fresh or thawed frozen

substitutions: Use apples, pears, or thawed frozen berries instead of peaches.
Use white sugar instead of brown sugar.
Use quick oats if that is what you have.

steps.text: Add the oat topping and bake.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 375°F. Put 2 cups sliced peaches in a small baking dish and sprinkle with 1 tablespoon brown sugar.
Mix 1/2 cup oats, 1/4 cup flour, the remaining 1 tablespoon brown sugar, 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, and 3 tablespoons softened butter until crumbly. Scatter over the peaches.
Bake 22–25 minutes, until the fruit bubbles and the topping is lightly browned.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat briefly or eat chilled.
